'''Corey James Kispert''' (born March 3, 1999) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Atlanta Hawks]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga Bulldogs]], where he was a consensus first-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] as a senior.

==Early life and high school career==
Kispert grew up in [[Edmonds, Washington]] and attended [[King's High School]]. As a junior, he averaged 23.9 points, 6.8 rebounds, 3.4 assists and 2.3 steals per game, led the team to their second straight state title, and was named the MVP of the State Championship Tournament.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.spokesman.com/blogs/sportslink/2016/may/04/kispert-commits-gonzaga/|title=Kispert commits to Gonzaga|first=Jim|last=Meehan|work=The Spokesman-Review|date=May 4, 2016|access-date=December 26, 2019}}</ref> Rated a four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]], Kispert committed to playing [[college basketball]] for [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]] over [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball|Notre Dame]] after his junior season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://notredame.rivals.com/news/corey-kispert-sets-notre-dame-visit|title=Corey Kispert Sets Notre Dame Visit|first=Jordan|last=Wells|website=Rivals.com|date=April 7, 2016|access-date=December 26, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2638011-corey-kispert-to-gonzaga-bulldogs-land-4-star-sf-prospect|title=Corey Kispert to Gonzaga: Bulldogs Land 4-Star SF Prospect|first=Scott|last=Polacek|website=[[Bleacher Report]]|date=May 4, 2016|access-date=December 26, 2019}}</ref> Kispert was averaging 25 points per game during his senior year before breaking his foot in February.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/high-school/kings-corey-kispert-a-gonzaga-signee-out-for-season-with-broken-bone-in-foot/|title=King’s Corey Kispert, a Gonzaga signee, out for season with broken bone in foot|first=Sandy|last=Ringer|work=The Seattle Times|date=February 19, 2017|access-date=December 26, 2019}}</ref>

Kispert said in 2021 that [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia]] head coach [[Tony Bennett (basketball)|Tony Bennett]] told Kispert he "needed to see Corey play more against top competition before deciding if he could play at Virginia" and that motivated him to "stick it to" Virginia in an early season game; Virginia had recruited Kispert but did not offer him a scholarship before he committed to Gonzaga.<ref>"[https://www.essentiallysports.com/ncaa-college-basketball-news-gonzaga-bulldogs-corey-kispert-reveals-how-virginia-cavaliers-tony-bennett-motivated-him-to-kick-their-a/ Corey Kispert Claims Tony Bennett Told Him He Wasn't Good Enough To Play, So Kispert Dropped 32 Against Virginia To 'Stick It To Him']". Essentially Sports, April 22, 2021. Accessed April 22, 2021.</ref>

==College career==
As a true freshman, Kispert played in all 35 of Gonzaga's games with seven starts, averaging 6.7 points and 3.2 rebounds per game.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.slipperstillfits.com/2019/10/8/20904190/2019-20-player-preview-corey-kispert|title=2019-20 Player Preview: Corey Kispert|website=SlipperStillFits.com|first=Megan|last=Stoudt|date=October 8, 2019|access-date=December 26, 2019}}</ref> He became a starter for the Bulldogs going into his sophomore season, averaging eight points and 4.1 rebounds per game.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/gonzaga-bulldogs/edmonds-native-corey-kispert-has-been-a-difference-maker-for-gonzaa-oh-yeah-and-hes-got-great-hair/|title=Edmonds native Corey Kispert has been a difference maker for Gonzaga. Oh yeah, and he’s got great hair.|first=Matt|last=Calkins|work=The Seattle Times|date=March 28, 2019|access-date=December 26, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/1294674/2019/10/22/is-gonzagas-corey-kispert-ready-for-a-larger-offensive-role/|title=Is Gonzaga’s Corey Kispert ready for a larger offensive role?|first=Jackson|last=Frank|website=[[The Athletic]]|date=October 22, 2019|access-date=December 26, 2019}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Washington Wizards===
[[File:Corey Kispert (51827251346).jpg|thumb|right|Kispert shoots a free throw with the [[Washington Wizards]] in 2025]]
On July 29, 2021, Kispert was drafted with the 15th overall pick in the [[2021 NBA draft]] by the [[Washington Wizards]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Washington Wizards take Zags’ Corey Kispert with 15th pick |url=https://wtop.com/washington-wizards/2021/07/washington-wizards-take-zags-corey-kispert-with-15th-pick/ |access-date=July 30, 2021 |work=WTOP |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=July 30, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Wizards select Corey Kispert with 15th pick in 2021 NBA Draft|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/wizards-select-kispert-15th-pick-2021-nba-draft|access-date=July 31, 2021|website=NBA.com}}</ref> On August 4, he signed his rookie scale contract with the Wizards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Corey Kispert Signs Rookie Deal With Wizards |url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2021/08/corey-kispert-signs-rookie-deal-with-wizards.html |access-date=February 6, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> Kispert made his NBA debut on October 22, scoring two points in a 135–134 overtime win over the [[Indiana Pacers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=DINWIDDIE LEADS WIZARDS TO 135-134 OT WIN OVER PACERS |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022100019 |access-date=February 6, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> In his rookie year with the Wizards he averaged 8.2 points per game, in his second year he averaged 11.1 points per game, and in his third year he averaged 13.4 points per game.<ref name="NBA.REF">{{Cite web |title=Corey Kispert Stats |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/k/kispeco01.html |access-date=January 25, 2025 |website=Basketball-Reference.com}}</ref>

Kispert is known as an excellent three-point shooter <ref>{{Cite web |title=Could Rockets trade for Wizards veteran? |url=https://www.si.com/nba/rockets/news/could-houston-rockets-trade-for-wizards-veteran-corey-kispert |access-date=January 17, 2025 |website=www.si.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=What Can NBA's Best Three-Point Shooters Tell Us About Corey Kispert's Future?|url=https://www.nbcwashington.com/news/local/what-can-nbas-best-three-point-shooters-tell-us-about-corey-kisperts-future/3132262/ |access-date=August 12, 2022 |website=nbcwashington.com}}</ref> and currently (January 2025) has a 38.2% career three-point percentage.<ref name="NBA.REF" /> In his second year with the Wizards, his three-point percentage was 42.4%, which was 10th best in the league. In a game against the [[Orlando Magic]] on March 31, 2023, he made 9 of 14 three-pointers (64.3%) on the way to scoring 27 points.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Orlando Magic at Washington Wizards box score, March 31, 2023 |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/202303310WAS.html |access-date=January 25, 2025 |website=Basketball-Reference.com}}</ref> The 9 three-pointers tie him for 2nd-most three-pointers in a game in franchise history.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Most 3 pointers scored by a Washington Wizards player in a single game|url=https://www.statmuse.com/nba/ask/most-3-pointers-scored-by-a-washington-wizards-player-in-a-single-game |access-date=January 25, 2025 |website=statmuse.com}}</ref>

On October 21, 2024, Kispert and the Wizards agreed to a four–year, $54 million contract extension.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Wizards, Corey Kispert agree to 4-year, $54M extension|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/41929354/wizards-corey-kispert-agree-4-year-54m-extension|access-date=October 22, 2024|website=espn.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Reports: Wizards, Corey Kispert agree to 4-year contract extension|url=https://www.nba.com/news/wizards-corey-kispert-extension|access-date=October 22, 2024|website=nba.com|language=en}}</ref> In 61 appearances for Washington, he averaged 11.6 points, 3.0 rebounds, and 1.7 assists. On March 18, 2025, it was announced that Kispert would miss the remainder of the season after undergoing surgery to repair a torn ligament in his left thumb.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 18, 2025 |title=Wiz's Kispert out for season after thumb surgery |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/44305845/wizards-corey-kispert-thumb-surgery-season |access-date=2025-12-07 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref>

Kispert made 19 appearances (two starts) for Washington during the [[2025–26 NBA season]], averaging 9.2 points, 2.3 rebounds, and 1.7 assists. On November 27, 2025, Kispert was ruled out after being diagnosed with a fracture in the tip of his right thumb.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Wizards Forward Suffers Thumb Fracture|url=https://www.si.com/nba/wizards/onsi/washington-wizards-news/washington-wizards-corey-krispert-suffers-thumb-fracture|access-date=January 20, 2026|website=si.com|language=en}}</ref>

===Atlanta Hawks===
On January 9, 2026, Kispert, alongside [[CJ McCollum]], was traded to the [[Atlanta Hawks]] in exchange for [[Trae Young]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Atlanta Hawks Acquire CJ Mccollum, Corey Kispert From Washington In Exchange For Trae Young |url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-acquire-cj-mccollum-corey-kispert-from-washington-in-exchange-for-trae-young |website=NBA.com |access-date=January 9, 2026 |date=January 9, 2026}}</ref> On February 26, Kispert recorded a career-high 33 points and six rebounds in a 126–96 victory over the [[2025–26 Washington Wizards season|Washington Wizards]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Gonzaga great Corey Kispert scores career-high 33 points in win over former team|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/gonzaga-great-corey-kispert-scores-045900463.html|access-date=April 27, 2026|website=sports.yahoo.com|language=en}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Kispert is a [[Catholic Church|Catholic]]. While at Gonzaga, Kispert met his girlfriend Jenn Wirth, where they both played basketball. The couple got married on July 7, 2023, at the [[Mission Basilica San Juan Capistrano]] in [[San Juan Capistrano, California]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Chandonnet |first=Henry |last2=Strohm |first2=Emily |date=July 15, 2023 |title=Wizards' Corey Kispert Marries Gonzaga College Sweetheart Jenn Wirth: 'Meant to be Together' (Exclusive) |url=https://people.com/wizards-corey-kispert-marries-gonzaga-college-sweetheart-jenn-wirth-exclusive-7557565 |access-date=July 16, 2023 |website=Peoplemag |language=en}}</ref> He is the grandson of [[Dainard Paulson]], a former [[American Football League]] player who holds that league's record for most [[Interception|interceptions]] in a season.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Ogden |first=Whitney |date=December 24, 2017 |title=Zags' Kispert selected basketball despite wishes of grandfather who played in NFL |work=The Spokesman-Review (Spokane, Washington) |pages=B-1}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=NFL Interceptions Single-Season Leaders (since 1940) |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/leaders/def_int_single_season.htm |access-date=2025-11-16 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>
